incidents.name: taikotalent.xyz fake-recruiter terminal trojan
incidents.cause_of_death: Registrar clientHold ~12 hours after evidence-backed abuse reports (AWS case 179121234700301, NameCheap ticket NC-DFA-2100, 13 notified channels)
incidents.epitaph: It asked developers to paste a downloader into their own terminal. No exploit was needed; the user executed the malware themselves.
incidents.vector: Fake 'Engineering opening' recruiting emails sent to developers harvested from public GitHub profiles; a fake application portal; an 'Anti-bot check with Terminal' page; self-executed downloader
incidents.residue: C2 domains api.gaganata.ink and api.fallgganata.ink were still answering at disclosure time; reports remain pending

lessons.lesson: An agent can correctly recognize a threat and still take an external action it was never authorized to take. Recognition and permission are different faculties.
The dangerous step was an ordinary terminal command typed by a trusting user. The failure point is authority, not capability.
An approval that lives forever is not consent. Authority must expire, because the context that justified it expires.
Consent for one action is not consent for a similar action. Approval binds to a digest of the exact tool and arguments, and a mismatch consumes the capability.
An effect that cannot be shown to a human before it happens should not happen. Every external effect in this project is simulated.
Open evidence took the domain down in about twelve hours. Decisions should leave verifiable traces, signed and independent of the process that made them.
A model may explain a decision in its own words, but it must never be able to grant permission or change policy.
